disclaimer: Informational only. Not a diagnosis, not a prediction of an individual reaction, and not a guarantee that a product is safe.
precautionary_pattern: may contain|traces? of|(manufactured|processed|made|produced) in a facility

milk.name: Milk / Dairy
milk.basics: Milk allergy is an immune reaction to milk proteins, not to lactose sugar (intolerance).
milk.science: Casein is heat-stable; baking rarely removes it.
milk.cross_reacts_with: Goat and sheep milk; beef in select patients

peanut.name: Peanut / Groundnut
peanut.protein: Storage proteins Ara h 1, Ara h 2, Ara h 3
peanut.basics: Peanut is a legume. Its storage proteins withstand high baking temperatures and gastric digestion.
peanut.science: Ara h 2 is a major biomarker linked to systemic reactions.

tree.name: Tree Nuts
tree.protein: 2S albumins and vicilins (e.g. Ana o 3 in cashew)
tree.basics: Tree nut allergy involves storage albumins that are highly conserved across species.
tree.science: Cashew and pistachio share closely homologous proteins.

egg.name: Eggs
egg.basics: Most egg allergens are in the albumen. Ovomucoid is heat-stable.
egg.science: "Albumin" or "lysozyme" on ingredients is often egg-derived.

fish.name: Fish
fish.basics: Parvalbumin is heat-resistant and survives boiling and frying.
fish.science: High structural homology across teleost fishes explains cross-reactivity.

shell.name: Crustaceans / Shellfish
shell.basics: Tropomyosin is pan-allergenic across crustaceans and molluscs.
shell.science: Conserved helical coiled-coil structure causes cross-reaction with house-dust mites.

peanuts.name: Peanuts
peanuts.protein: Storage proteins Ara h 1, Ara h 2, Ara h 3, Ara h 6
peanuts.basics: Peanuts contain heat-stable 2S albumin and cupin seed storage proteins.
peanuts.science: Ara h 2 and Ara h 6 resist pepsin digestion and thermal processing.
peanuts.cross_reacts_with: Lupin, soybean, chickpea, and tree nuts (co-sensitization)

soy.name: Soy
soy.protein: Glycinin (Gly m 6), β-conglycinin (Gly m 5), Gly m 4
soy.basics: Soy proteins are ubiquitous in emulsifiers, sauces, and processed goods.
soy.science: Refined soy oil has minimal protein, but soy flour/lecithin contain triggers.
soy.cross_reacts_with: Other legumes, including peanut, chickpea, and lentil

wheat_plain.name: Wheat
wheat_plain.protein: Tri a 14 (LTP), Tri a 19 (omega-5 gliadin), Tri a 36
wheat_plain.basics: IgE-mediated wheat allergy targets water-soluble albumins, globulins, and gliadins in wheat grain.
wheat_plain.science: Omega-5 gliadin (Tri a 19) is a major marker for wheat-dependent exercise-induced anaphylaxis.
wheat_plain.cross_reacts_with: Durum, spelt, kamut, triticale, barley, rye

wheat.name: Wheat / Gluten
wheat.protein: Gliadins, glutenins and wheat albumins (Tri a 19, Tri a 14)
wheat.basics: Wheat allergy is an IgE reaction, whereas gluten sensitivity/coeliac disease targets prolamin peptides.
wheat.science: Barley hordein and rye secalin share homologous gluten epitopes with wheat gliadin.
wheat.cross_reacts_with: Barley, rye, triticale; grass pollen in oral allergy syndrome

sesame.name: Sesame
sesame.protein: Seed storage 2S albumins & 11S globulins (Ses i 1, Ses i 2, Ses i 6)
sesame.basics: Common in tahini, baked goods, hummus, burger buns, and Asian oil blends.
sesame.science: Sesame oleosins and 2S albumins are highly lipophilic and heat-resistant.
sesame.cross_reacts_with: Poppy seed, hazelnut, walnut, and peanut in select cases

chickpea.name: Chickpea
chickpea.protein: Cic a 1, 7S vicilin & 2S albumin storage proteins
chickpea.basics: Chickpea (Bengal gram) is a major legume allergen in South Asian and Mediterranean diets, often hidden as besan or aquafaba.
chickpea.science: Chickpea 2S albumins and 7S vicilins retain IgE-binding epitopes after boiling and frying.
chickpea.cross_reacts_with: Lentil, pea, lupin, soy, and peanut

lentils.name: Lentils
lentils.protein: Len c 1 (gamma-vicilin), Len c 2, Len c 3 (lipid transfer protein)
lentils.basics: Lentils are a frequent trigger of legume-induced anaphylaxis in pediatric and adult populations across India and the Mediterranean.
lentils.science: Len c 1 vicilin subunits are highly stable against thermal denaturation and digestive enzymes.
lentils.cross_reacts_with: Chickpea, green pea, peanut, and lupin

mushrooms.name: Mushrooms
mushrooms.protein: Ribosomal protein, enolase, mannitol dehydrogenase & trehalose
mushrooms.basics: Edible fungi can cause both IgE-mediated food allergy and lentinan-induced toxic/inflammatory dermatitis (shiitake flagellate erythema).
mushrooms.science: Fungal enolases and heat-shock proteins share conserved structures with airborne mold spores.
mushrooms.cross_reacts_with: Airborne molds (Alternaria, Cladosporium, Aspergillus) and nutritional yeast

beef.name: Beef
beef.protein: Bos d 6 (bovine serum albumin), Bos d 7 (IgG) & Galactose-α-1,3-galactose (Alpha-Gal)
beef.basics: Beef allergy can arise from primary sensitization to bovine serum albumin or tick-bite-induced Alpha-Gal syndrome (delayed anaphylaxis).
beef.science: Bos d 6 is partially heat-labile (well-done beef is sometimes tolerated), whereas Alpha-Gal glycolipids survive cooking.
beef.cross_reacts_with: Cow milk (in Bos d 6 sensitization); pork, lamb, and mammalian gelatin

pork.name: Pork
pork.protein: Sus s 1 (porcine serum albumin) & Alpha-Gal carbohydrate
pork.basics: Pork allergy occurs via primary sensitization, Alpha-Gal syndrome, or "Pork-Cat Syndrome" (cross-sensitization to cat Fel d 2 albumin).
pork.science: Sus s 1 serum albumin denatures partially with prolonged heat, so cured/smoked meats (bacon, ham) pose higher reactivity.
pork.cross_reacts_with: Cat dander (Fel d 2), beef, lamb, and mammalian gelatin

chicken.name: Chicken
chicken.protein: Gal d 5 (alpha-livetin / serum albumin), Gal d 7 (myosin light chain) & Gal d 8 (parvalbumin)
chicken.basics: Primary chicken meat allergy involves muscle myosin and parvalbumin, whereas secondary "Bird-Egg Syndrome" targets Gal d 5.
chicken.science: Gal d 7 and Gal d 8 are heat-stable muscle allergens that persist in cooked poultry broths and stocks.
chicken.cross_reacts_with: Turkey, duck, pheasant; egg yolk (in Bird-Egg Syndrome)

perilla.name: Perilla Seeds
perilla.protein: Perilla oleosins (14–16 kDa) & 2S seed storage albumins
perilla.basics: Perilla seed is an emerging high-risk seed allergen widely used in Korean, Japanese, and Chinese cuisines (oils, powders, and marinades).
perilla.science: Lipophilic oleosin proteins partition into cold-pressed perilla oil and resist standard aqueous extraction.
perilla.cross_reacts_with: Sesame seed and other Lamiaceae herbs

almonds.name: Almonds
almonds.protein: Pru du 6 (amandin / 11S legumin), Pru du 3 (LTP) & Pru du 4 (profilin)
almonds.basics: Almond is a Rosaceae drupe seed classified among tree nuts. Reactions range from oral allergy syndrome to severe systemic anaphylaxis.
almonds.science: Pru du 6 (amandin) accounts for ~65% of soluble almond protein and is highly resistant to dry roasting.
almonds.cross_reacts_with: Peach, apricot, cherry, plum (Rosaceae family), and other tree nuts

walnuts.name: Walnuts
walnuts.protein: Jug r 1 (2S albumin), Jug r 2 (7S vicilin), Jug r 3 (LTP) & Jug r 4 (11S legumin)
walnuts.basics: Walnut is one of the most potent tree nut triggers, frequently causing systemic reactions at trace milligram exposures.
walnuts.science: Jug r 1 is a compact disulfide-bridged 2S albumin that remains intact through baking and gastric acid.
walnuts.cross_reacts_with: Pecan (strong ~90% clinical cross-reactivity), hazelnut, and Brazil nut

kiwi.name: Kiwi
kiwi.protein: Act d 1 (actinidin cysteine protease), Act d 2 (thaumatin-like), Act d 5 (kiwellin) & Act d 8 (PR-10)
kiwi.basics: Kiwifruit causes both localized oral allergy symptoms and severe systemic reactions, especially in young children.
kiwi.science: Act d 1 is an abundant proteolytic enzyme that resists gastrointestinal breakdown and disrupts epithelial tight junctions.
kiwi.cross_reacts_with: Natural rubber latex, banana, avocado, chestnut (Latex-Fruit Syndrome); birch pollen

apples.name: Apples
apples.protein: Mal d 1 (PR-10 Bet v 1 homolog), Mal d 2 (thaumatin-like) & Mal d 3 (non-specific LTP)
apples.basics: Apple allergy presents as pollen-food syndrome (Mal d 1, mild oral itching) or primary Mediterranean-type anaphylaxis (Mal d 3 in peel).
apples.science: Mal d 1 is heat-labile (cooked apple pie is often tolerated), whereas peel-concentrated Mal d 3 survives pasteurization.
apples.cross_reacts_with: Birch pollen, pear, peach, cherry, hazelnut, celery, and carrot

peach.name: Peach
peach.protein: Pru p 3 (non-specific lipid transfer protein), Pru p 1 (PR-10) & Pru p 7 (gibberellin-regulated protein)
peach.basics: Peach is the classic sensitizer for Lipid Transfer Protein (LTP) syndrome, with allergens heavily concentrated in the fuzzy outer skin.
peach.science: Pru p 3 features four disulfide bridges forming a rigid alpha-helical tunnel that survives canning, jamming, and pepsin.
peach.cross_reacts_with: Apricot, plum, cherry, almond, apple, walnut, and mugwort pollen

barley.name: Barley
barley.protein: Hor v 15 (alpha-amylase inhibitor), Hor v 20 (gamma-3 hordein) & Hor v 16
barley.basics: Barley prolamins (hordeins) trigger both IgE-mediated baker/food allergy (commonly via beer or malt extract) and coeliac disease.
barley.science: Barley lipid transfer protein (Hor v 14) and gamma-3 hordein survive malting, brewing, and baking processes.
barley.cross_reacts_with: Wheat, rye, oats, triticale, and beer/malt beverages

alcohol.name: Alcohol
alcohol.protein: Ethanol / Acetaldehyde (ALDH2 pathway), Biogenic Histamines, Sulfites & Residual LTPs (Vit v 1 / Hor v 14)
alcohol.basics: Reactions to alcoholic beverages involve ALDH2 metabolic flushing, sulfite/histamine intolerance, or true IgE allergy to grape/barley/yeast proteins.
alcohol.science: Ethanol increases gut mucosal permeability, accelerating systemic absorption of co-ingested food allergens.
alcohol.cross_reacts_with: Wine vinegar, fermented sauces (mirin, cooking wine), grapes, barley malt, and baker yeast

melon.name: Melon
melon.protein: Cuc m 1 (cucumisin serine protease), Cuc m 2 (profilin) & Cuc m 3 (PR-1 protein)
melon.basics: Melon allergy is strongly associated with ragweed and grass pollen sensitization, typically triggering rapid oral pruritus and angioedema.
melon.science: Cuc m 2 profilin is sensitive to gastric pepsin, while Cuc m 1 protease exhibits higher structural stability.
melon.cross_reacts_with: Watermelon, cucumber, zucchini (Cucurbitaceae); banana, avocado, ragweed pollen

banana.name: Banana
banana.protein: Mus a 1 (profilin), Mus a 2 (class I chitinase), Mus a 3 (LTP) & Mus a 4 (thaumatin-like)
banana.basics: Banana is a key component of Latex-Fruit Syndrome due to hevein-like chitinase domains shared with natural rubber latex.
banana.science: Mus a 2 class I chitinase contains an N-terminal hevein domain that cross-links latex-specific IgE antibodies.
banana.cross_reacts_with: Natural rubber latex, avocado, kiwi, chestnut, and melon

watermelon.name: Watermelon
watermelon.protein: Cit l 1 (malate dehydrogenase), Cit l 2 (profilin) & Cit l 3 (triosephosphate isomerase)
watermelon.basics: Watermelon allergy commonly affects individuals sensitized to ragweed or grass pollens, causing oral allergy syndrome or urticaria.
watermelon.science: Pan-allergen profilin (Cit l 2) shares >80% sequence identity with ragweed Amb a 8 and melon Cuc m 2.
watermelon.cross_reacts_with: Cantaloupe, honeydew melon, cucumber, zucchini, banana, and ragweed pollen

mango.name: Mango
mango.protein: Man i 1 (class I chitinase), Man i 2, Man i 4 (profilin) & Urushiol-like alk(en)ylresorcinols
mango.basics: Mango causes both immediate IgE anaphylaxis (pulp proteins) and delayed Type IV perioral contact dermatitis ("mango rash" from peel sap).
mango.science: Mango belongs to the Anacardiaceae family; sap resorcinols cross-react with poison ivy urushiol, while seed/pulp proteins relate to cashew.
mango.cross_reacts_with: Cashew, pistachio, pink peppercorn (Anacardiaceae); mugwort pollen, birch pollen, and latex

duck.name: Duck
duck.protein: Anatidae alpha-livetin (serum albumin), myosin light chain & parvalbumin
duck.basics: Duck meat and duck egg reactions occur via primary avian muscle sensitization or secondary Bird-Egg Syndrome.
duck.science: Avian serum albumins and muscle alpha-parvalbumins show cross-species conservation across waterfowl and landfowl.
duck.cross_reacts_with: Chicken, turkey, goose, quail meat, and avian eggs

berries.name: Berries
berries.protein: Fra a 1 (PR-10 Bet v 1 homolog), Fra a 3 (LTP), Fra a 4 (profilin) & Rub i 1
berries.basics: Strawberries and Cane/Vaccinium berries contain PR-10 and lipid transfer proteins as well as natural salicylates and histamine liberators.
berries.science: Fra a 1 expression is linked to red anthocyanin ripening pathways; white strawberry cultivars have markedly lower Fra a 1 levels.
berries.cross_reacts_with: Birch pollen, apple, peach, cherry, rose hips, and other Rosaceae fruits

garlic.name: Garlic
garlic.protein: All s 1 (alliin lyase, 50 kDa) & diallyl disulfide-haptenated proteins
garlic.basics: Garlic (Allium sativum) can trigger IgE-mediated occupational asthma, contact dermatitis, and systemic gastrointestinal/anaphylactic reactions.
garlic.science: Alliin lyase (All s 1) is an abundant vacuolar glycoprotein that cross-reacts across Allium species.
garlic.cross_reacts_with: Onion, leek, chive, shallot, scallion (Allium genus), and asparagus

corn.name: Corn
corn.protein: Zea m 14 (non-specific lipid transfer protein, 9 kDa) & Zea m 25 (thioredoxin)
corn.basics: Corn/maize allergy is challenging to manage because corn derivatives (starches, syrups, flours) are ubiquitous in processed foods.
corn.science: Zea m 14 is an extremely heat- and acid-stable lipid transfer protein that survives nixtamalization and baking.
corn.cross_reacts_with: Rice, wheat, barley, sorghum, millet, peach (via LTP), and grass pollens

oats.name: Oats
oats.protein: Avenin prolamins & Ave s 12S globulin storage proteins
oats.basics: Oats cause both IgE-mediated food/contact allergies and FPIES, and are frequently cross-contaminated with wheat/barley in shared mills.
oats.science: Pure avenin lacks the main immunodominant coeliac 33-mer gliadin peptide, but still triggers reactions in ~5-8% of coeliac and oat-allergic patients.
oats.cross_reacts_with: Wheat, barley, rye, rice, and grass pollen

peanut.title: Ara h 2 (peanut)
peanut.note: Often described as a major peanut allergen. Verify ID before final use.

milk.title: Bos d 5 (beta-lactoglobulin)
milk.note: Major whey protein in cow milk.

shell.title: Pen a 1 (shrimp tropomyosin)
shell.note: Conservation across species is why cross-reactivity is discussed. Verify ID before final use.

sample_label: Wheat flour (maida), sugar, palm oil, milk solids, soy lecithin, cashew paste, salt, natural flavour. May contain peanuts and sesame.
